messages:
Alex: spotted a customer complaint: they see double token charges when a stream falls back to the compact model mid-toolcall. repro attached.
Priya: can you paste the sequence? iirc toolcalls are charged on finalization, but streaming + fallback might be emitting partials?
Alex: sequence: client opens stream -> router picks model-full -> model-full starts emitting streaming tokens and sends an in-progress toolcall payload -> router decides to fallback to model-compact due to burst policy -> fallback triggers reconnect to compact and the compact instance replays suffix including a final toolcall finalize. result: two finalizations recorded.
Jordan: oh that path is nasty. does the router dedupe toolcall_final events by session token?
Alex: not today. we only dedupe based on `client_request_id` for non-streaming toolcalls. Streaming finalization currently lacks a stable id across model handoffs.
Priya: schematic:
```
[client] -> stream(session=abc)
[router] -> model-full (handler A)
[model-full] emits: toolcall(in_progress) prefix=...
[router] fallback to model-compact -> new connection handler B
[model-compact] emits: suffix + toolcall(final) -> billing sees final
[handler A] eventually emits final for the original inflight chunk -> billing sees final again
```
Alex: billing sees two final events spaced ~120ms apart. both considered confirmed. customer gets charged twice for the same tool invocation.
Jordan: we should add a stable stream-session-id that follows the logical session across handoffs and include it on toolcall final events. billing should dedupe on (customer_id, stream_session_id, toolcall_hash).
Priya: agree. low-risk mitigation: when fallback happens, router can send a cancel/abort to the original handler and ensure it won't emit a final; but some model runtimes don't support cancel reliably.
Alex: also saw edge case where the handler that was aborted still flushes its local queue on shutdown and emits final. so router-level cancel isn't sufficient unless the runtime guarantees no flush on abort.
Jordan: proposal: 1) introduce `session_trace_id` injected at router start and propagated to every model handler and emitted events. 2) billing/billing-proxy dedupe final toolcalls if they share session_trace_id + toolcall_sha256. 3) console show a new row in the per-route billing table named `deduped_toolcall_fallbacks` and an alert if > 0.1% of toolcalls for a route in 1h window.
cost-bot: Alert created CB-998: deduped_toolcall_fallbacks > 0.1% on eu-central for the last 30m.
Priya: rough effort: router change + header plumbing ~2d, model handler libs update (go/python) ~2d, billing dedupe logic + tests ~3d, console + alert ~1d. total ~8d.
Alex: short term workaround: mark the second final with a provisional tag when it arrives <500ms after another final with same toolcall hash, and queue it for reconcile instead of immediate charge. That reduces customer-impact while we ship the full dedupe.
Jordan: reconcile job design: scan confirmed-final events, group by (customer, toolcall_hash) with time window 1s, if more than one, keep the earliest as confirmed and mark others as refunded/provisional. write to billing adjustments table and emit an annotation to the invoice pipeline.
Priya: can we implement the provisional tag in billing-proxy without changing upstream handlers? yes, we can use short-lived cache keyed by (customer, toolcall_hash) with TTL=2s. if we see a final and cache hit, treat as provisional.
Alex: i'll open an RFC PR outlining session_trace_id and billing dedupe semantics. link incoming.
Alex: RFC: https://git.internal/redwood/rfcs/pull/512 (contains sequence diagrams and compatibility notes)
deploybot: staging deploy started for billing-proxy@pr-210
Jordan: Can we also add an observability trace that annotates handoffs so we can retroactively find customers impacted? e.g., a span tag `fallback=true` with reason.
Priya: yes, trace annotation is cheap and helps runbook. console runbook: steps to identify impacted customers, run reconcile, and issue credits. Add quick-button in the per-customer billing view to launch reconcile for a time window.
Alex: i'll add the trace annotations in the router PR. planning canary: 3% traffic to router with session_trace_id + billing-proxy provisional cache; monitor CB-998 alert and invoice delta. expand to 25% -> 100% if stable.
Jordan: testing: unit tests for dedupe, an e2e with simulated fallback where both handlers attempt final, assert single confirmed charge. also a chaos test killing handler A mid-final.
Priya: assigned owners: router (Alex), billing-proxy (Jordan), billing team review (me). timeline: target ship in 2 sprints.
Alex: thanks. i'll post PRs tomorrow and add the canary checklist. :thumbsup: 
Jordan: :eyes:
